chapter_theme: Songs to Vinayaka (விநாயகர்): prayers to the elephant-faced god for grace and a mind fixed on worship, one ritual offering ending in a battlefield, and a first confession of being sunk in women's love.
structure_note: 3 is a short plea and praise; 4 sets a worship scene against a battle scene; 5 has the book's usual two halves, a confession about women and a praise whose story is obscure. All three end at Ganapati.

3.reading: The poet asks Ganapati to melt for him like the wish-granting tree, cow and gem of the gods, to let him drink the nectar of bliss many times, and to give his life grace. He praises him as the one who went to the forest for his younger brother's sake, who won the fruit by circling his father, the substance of those who love him, the five-handed elephant face.
3.nuance: தம்பிதனக்காக வனத்தணைவோனே recalls the elephant in Valli's forest (see 1). தந்தைவலத்தால் அருள் கைக்கனியோனே is the fruit won by going round the father, the story in which Murugan circles the world (30).

4.reading: The poet says he will never forget to worship the elephant-faced one with the single tusk, setting out fruits, appam, milk, honey, sugarcane, laddus, rice, dal, aval, sesame, plantains and tender coconut, with hymns, holding his ears, sit-ups and knocks on the temples, before the anklet-bearing lotus feet, so that he is given a mind that keeps the Lord's feet in thought. The second half is a battlefield: flies swarm on rivers of blood, flesh, bile, fat and brains, drums and tabors thunder, ghouls clap, Bhairavi dances in a ring, and the Lord offers the night-walking demons as sacrifice.
4.nuance: குழைபிடி தொப்பண குட்டொடு names the gestures still made before Ganapati: holding the ears, sit-ups (தோப்புக்கரணம்) and knocking the temples. The battle half is sung in drum syllables (தெனன, திமித, டிமுட), a device used again in 6 and 11. Whether the closing பெருமாளே is Ganapati, as the heading implies, or Murugan, the song does not settle.

5.reading: The poet confesses that, not knowing what deeds yield, he has drowned day and night in lovemaking on fragrant beds with women whose eyes are like the poison-filled sea, the gods' weapons, the trident and Vijaya's arrow, a base and ignorant wretch; he asks that he too be granted the Lord's anklets. The praise tells a story in which cowherds steal a little milk, a lord's daughter, not knowing the truth, cries out to 'my child, Ganapati', and the elephant-faced god gives understanding.
5.nuance: வினையின் விளைவு ஏதும் அறியாதே: the fault confessed is ignorance of what deeds bring. The second half's story is not one I can identify, and the lines (அகல்வதென் டாசொல் எனவுமுடி சாட) are hard to divide; the reading of the praise is a guess.

links.note: Thiruppugazh 3 praises Ganapati as the one who won the fruit by going round his father (தந்தைவலத்தால் அருள் கைக்கனியோனே). Thiruppugazh 176 tells the loser's side: Hara gave the fruit to the elephant-faced one (அந்தப் பலனைக் கரிமுகன் வசம் அருளும்) while Murugan circled the golden mountain, and Murugan, angry, went to Palani. The same contest is a title of honour in the one song and the origin of a shrine in the other.

Thiruppugazh 3 names Ganapati by the circling of his father that won him the fruit. Thiruppugazh 153 sets the two circlings side by side: the elephant-faced one runs round Hara (ஆனைமுகர் அரனை ஓடி வலம்வரு முன்) while Murugan's peacock goes round the sea-girt world (உலகை வலமாக வரு துரக மயில்வீரா). Read together, the two songs give both halves of the contest that 3 compresses into one epithet.

Thiruppugazh 4 lays out the offerings to the single-tusked elephant face (fruit, appam, aval, sesame, puffed rice, plantains, tender coconut) and asks that it give a mind that thinks of Murugan's feet, vel and peacock (நினது திருவடி சத்தி மயிற்கொடி நினைவு கருதிடு புத்தி). Thiruppugazh 1002 lists nearly the same offerings (கடலை பயறொடு துவரை ... அவல் பொரி ... கதலி) and then names Murugan as the one who comes after (பிறகு வருமொரு முருக), confessing failure to bow to him. Both make Ganapati's worship the step before Murugan's; 1002 turns that order into the poet's fault.

source_issues: Song 4: one corrupt character in செற஧முளை (line 15); probably செறிமூளை (packed brain).
